whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as 6 months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the accident, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't artificially capped.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Our team works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no hourly fee and no retainer required to get started.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in La Mirada?
items.answer: California generally allows 2 years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government agency, such as a city road or public vehicle, the notice period can be as short as 6 months, so it's wise to act early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in La Mirada?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Imperial Highway, Rosecrans Avenue, La Mirada Boulevard, and Valley View Avenue, with reports often peaking Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I owe anything if I don't win my case?
items.answer: No. Our team works on contingency, which means we only collect a fee if you recover money through a settlement or verdict.

items.answer: Yes. We handle personal injury cases and can review your situation to explain your options under California law. There's no cost to contact us, and we work on contingency — no fee unless you recover.
